publicPrompt:
Repair the paused/resumed and dynamically resized fastq callback/promise work queue. The full pinned repository lives in src/, including its existing upstream tests and docs. This fixture contains explicitly injected production defects; it is not a claim about an upstream release. A local reusify import is already wired to the full pinned dependency at src/vendor/reusify. Edit only src/queue.js. Use Node native tests; do not install dependencies or execute package scripts. Run node --test tests/visible.test.mjs from this workspace. Existing upstream tests need development dependencies and are provided as source context only. Passing visible tests is a regression floor; satisfy every behavioral requirement below.

F-R1: pause() prevents new workers from starting, including when concurrency is assigned a larger value. Already running work may complete while paused; its completion must reduce running(), leave waiting tasks in place, and not start waiting work.

F-R2: resume() changes a paused queue to unpaused and immediately fills every free worker slot up to concurrency, while preserving the count of already running workers. It starts no work when existing running workers already fill the limit. Calling resume() again on an unpaused queue has no effect.

F-R3: Waiting push() tasks start in FIFO order and unshift() places a waiting task ahead of them. Each task starts and completes exactly once, including when workers invoke their completion callback synchronously during resume(). running(), length(), getQueue(), and idle() must reflect the actual active and waiting tasks without lost or stranded work.

F-R4: When a worker finishes in an unpaused queue, the next waiting task immediately replaces it whenever the resulting active count is below concurrency; the queue must keep progressing without another push or resume. Raising concurrency on an unpaused queue immediately fills all newly free slots. Lowering it leaves active tasks running, prevents replacement while the active count would exceed the new limit, and resumes replacement once enough active workers finish.

F-R5: Retain callback/promise results and error behavior during queued execution: callbacks receive the original worker error and result and are called with the configured context; an installed error handler receives that task's error and original input. Synchronous and asynchronous workers both preserve those results. fastq.promise push()/unshift() promises must all settle with the matching worker results once work completes.

F-R6: empty() fires when dispatch removes the final waiting task; at that callback length() is zero. drain() fires once when a nonempty unpaused work batch becomes fully idle; at that callback running() is zero. No callback/result may be lost while scheduling and draining the batch.
